name: Plastic and reconstructive surgery
summary: How expats find board-certified plastic and reconstructive surgeons in Singapore for post-trauma repair, cancer reconstruction, scar revision, and elective aesthetic procedures — with clear medical vs cosmetic framing.
body:
Plastic surgery in Singapore spans reconstructive work (medically indicated) and aesthetic procedures (elective). Expats should separate the two for insurance, consent, and surgeon selection.

## Reconstructive indications
- Breast reconstruction after mastectomy
- Skin cancer excision with local or free-flap repair
- Hand trauma, tendon, and nerve repair (often shared with orthopaedic hand teams)
- Burn scar contracture release
- Congenital differences and complex wound coverage
- Post-weight-loss body contouring when medically documented

These pathways often start from oncology, orthopaedics, dermatology, or A&E. Public hospital plastic surgery departments handle major reconstruction; private consultants may offer earlier elective reconstructive slots.

## Aesthetic / elective
Rhinoplasty, blepharoplasty, facelift, liposuction, and similar procedures are widely available in private practice. Marketing can be loud — prioritise SMC-registered specialists in plastic surgery, facility accreditation, and realistic photography over social-media volume. Anaesthesia should be delivered in appropriately licensed day-surgery or hospital settings.

## Insurance and consent
Reconstructive procedures tied to cancer, trauma, or functional impairment may attract partial coverage; pure aesthetic work almost never does. Get written itemised quotes (surgeon, anaesthetist, facility, implants/meshes, follow-up). Ask about revision policies before paying deposits.

## How to choose
Verify specialist registration, hospital admitting rights for larger cases, and complication pathways. For reconstruction after cancer, prefer surgeons who sit in tumour-board pathways with your oncologist. For aesthetic work, insist on in-person consults, cooling-off time, and clear discussion of risks in your language.

## Practical tip
Avoid combining medical tourism haste with major elective surgery in the first weeks after landing — swelling follow-up, suture removal, and early complications are harder if you immediately travel again. Build at least local follow-up into the plan.
whenToEngage: When you need reconstruction after cancer or trauma, scar or wound problems your GP cannot manage, or you are evaluating elective aesthetic surgery and want specialist-credentialled care with clear facility standards.
